title: Exitwise wiki
intro: Every obstacle, powerup and rule in Exitwise: what it does, when it first shows up, and how to deal with it.
metaTitle: Exitwise wiki: every obstacle and powerup in the arrow puzzle
metaDescription: Every obstacle, powerup and rule in Exitwise, the free arrow puzzle game: what it does, the level it first shows up on, and how to beat it.
source: Written from the game on main (39aa208, 2026-10-17: the update with mirrors, portals, ice, shutters, the colour family and chain bombs). Later generated from Core's WikiCatalog.

sections.title: Obstacles
sections.intro: Things on the board that change where your arrows can go, and the arrows that deal with them. A new one arrives every 20 to 30 levels, starts on an easy level built to teach it, and then stays, mixed in with the ones before it.

sections.title: Powerups
sections.intro: One-tap helpers. You get 3 of each for free when it unlocks; more cost coins in the shop. None of them ever costs a heart, and none touches an arrow hidden under a shutter.

sections.title: Basics
sections.intro: How the game works: hearts, coins, hints, hard levels, worlds, and the ways to play with others.

entries.name: Rock
entries.summary: Stops every arrow until its bombs blow it up.
what: A rock is 1 to 4 connected cells that hold no arrow and stop every arrow that runs into it. It looks the same in every world: a warm stone with a dark outline. It stays until the bomb arrows aimed at it have hit it.
Arrows may point straight at a rock: they're blocked until it's gone.
how: Find the bomb whose path leads to the rock.
Clear the arrows in the bomb's way first, then tap the bomb.
Until then, plan around the rock: any arrow pointing at it bumps and costs a heart.
notes: Rocks first appear on level 21, where a short tutorial walks you through clearing a bomb's path and firing it.
Tougher rocks come later: level-2 rocks from level 81, level-3 rocks from 161, and whole rock walls from 281.

figure.alt: Level 25 in the Jungle: two stone rocks with dark outlines, and bomb arrows with round heads and fuses
figure.caption: Rocks and bomb arrows on level 25, in the Jungle.

script.say: The bomb’s path runs into the blue arrow: its guard.
Now the bomb flies to its rock.
The arrow behind the rock is free.

entries.name: Bomb arrow
entries.summary: Flies to its rock and blows it up, once its path is clear.
what: A bomb arrow looks like a bomb: a round charcoal head with a pointed nose that shows the way it flies, on a fuse with a flickering orange spark at the end. It looks the same on every board. Tap it and it flies along its path to the first rock and blows it up with a flash.
No bomb starts free: every bomb has a guard, an arrow standing on its path between the bomb and its rock. Clear the guard first, and whatever holds the guard up.
Bombs have no colour, so closed colour gates stop them, and so do arrows, ice and shutters. A blocked bomb bumps like any arrow and costs a heart.
how: Trace the bomb's path to its rock and find the arrow in the way.
Free that arrow, then tap the bomb.
Each bomb hits once: a level-2 or level-3 rock needs that many bombs, usually from different sides.
notes: The level-21 tutorial points out a rock ("New: rocks and bombs"), then the arrow in a bomb's way, then the bomb.

figure.alt: Level 25 in the Jungle: bomb arrows with round charcoal heads pointing the way they fly, fuses with orange sparks, and the rocks they're aimed at
figure.caption: Bomb arrows and their rocks on level 25.

facts: The first rock on its path

steps.text: Trace the bomb’s path to its rock and find the arrow in the way.
Free that arrow, then tap the bomb.
It flies along its path to the first rock and blows it up with a flash.

script.say: The bomb’s path runs into the blue arrow: its guard.
Now the bomb flies to its rock.
The arrow behind the rock is free.

tip.label: Tip
tip.title: Free the guard first
tip.text: No bomb starts free: clear its guard first, and whatever holds the guard up.

entries.name: Colour gate
entries.summary: Lets only its own colour through, then opens for good.
what: A gate is one cell in blue or yellow (purple from level 101), drawn as a coloured frame with a symbol: a circle, a triangle or a diamond, so you can match it without relying on colour.
An arrow of the gate's colour passes through and the gate opens behind it for good; after that every arrow gets through. Arrows of other colours, and bombs, bump into a closed gate.
how: Find the arrow with the gate's colour and symbol, and send it through first.
Later obstacles open gates too: a paint tile can give an arrow the gate's colour, and a key of its colour unlocks it at once (on a board with a key, its gates are drawn as locked doors).
notes: Gates first appear on level 41, with one gate and a free arrow of its colour heading through it.
In-game tip: "Only a gate's own colour gets through."

entries.name: Mirror
entries.summary: Turns an arrow's path by 90 degrees.
what: A mirror is one cell with a diagonal bar of glass, / or \. It holds no arrow and blocks nothing: an arrow whose path reaches it turns 90 degrees there and carries on.

A / turns a path heading right to go up, and one heading left to go down; a \ turns right into down and left into up. A path can bend more than once, and the arrow is free if the bent path is clear to the edge.
how: Follow the path, not the arrowhead: an arrow that looks blocked straight ahead may be free round the corner, and one that looks free may turn into a crowd.
Grid lines (the powerup) draw the bent paths for you.
notes: Mirrors first appear on level 61, three of them and nothing else; the tutorial taps an arrow that escapes round a bend.
In-game tip: "Mirrors turn arrows by 90 degrees."

figure.alt: Level 61 in the Volcano world: three diagonal glass mirrors among the arrows
figure.caption: Level 61 introduces mirrors.

entries.name: Level-2 rock
entries.summary: A tougher rock that takes two bomb hits.
what: A level-2 rock is darker stone with two white dots, one for each hit it still needs. Each bomb that hits it cracks it and takes a dot away; the second hit breaks it.
Its two bombs come from different arrows and, where the board allows, from different sides.
how: Count the dots: that's how many bombs you still have to free.
Look for the second bomb on another side of the rock before you plan the arrows behind it.
notes: Level 81 introduces them with two level-2 rocks and nothing else. After that about 15% of rocks are level 2, rising to 30% by level 160, and twice that share on hard levels.

figure.alt: Level 105 in the Lagoon: a T-shaped level-2 rock with two white dots among rocks, bomb arrows, a portal and mirrors
figure.caption: A level-2 rock (two dots) on level 105, with rocks, bombs and a portal.

entries.name: Portal
entries.summary: Carries an arrow's path across the board to its pair.
what: Portals come in pairs: a rim in the pair's colour round a dark, slowly turning swirl, with the pair's number as white dice dots (1 to 6). An arrow whose path reaches one portal sinks in, shoots out of its twin going the same way, and carries on.
Nothing rests on a portal and nothing is stopped by one. A pair's two cells are never in the same row or column.
how: When a path reaches a portal, jump to its twin (same colour, same dots) and keep following the path from there.
On a zoomed-in board the camera follows an escaping arrow through the portal, so you see where it comes out.
notes: Level 101 introduces portals with a single pair. Later levels have up to 6 pairs, each in its own colour.
In-game tip: "Portals send arrows out of their pair."

figure.alt: Level 101, the portals introduction: the card "New: portals" above a small board with its two green portals
figure.caption: Level 101 introduces portals: an arrow comes out of the twin with the same colour and dots.

facts: Up to 6, each in its own colour
Never in the same row or column

steps.text: An arrow whose path reaches one portal sinks in.
Jump to its twin: the same colour, the same dots.
It shoots out going the same way and carries on.

script.say: Follow the red arrow’s path: it reaches a portal.
It comes out of the twin and carries on.
Up into the twin, out of the first one.

tip.label: In the game
tip.title: New: portals
tip.text: An arrow that flies into a portal comes out of its twin, the one with the same colour and dots, going the same way.

entries.name: Ice
entries.summary: A block with a number that melts as arrows leave.
what: Ice is one cell showing a number. It holds no arrow and stops every arrow, bombs too, and a bomb can't break it.
Each time any arrow leaves the board, by a tap or a powerup, the number drops by one. At 0 the ice melts and the way is open.
how: Arrows pointing at the ice have to wait: clear the other arrows first.
The number is just big enough: the ice melts right as you run out of other arrows to clear, so spend your moves on the arrows that don't wait on it.
notes: Level 131 introduces ice with one block counting from 5, and a tutorial that shows an arrow waiting on it.
In-game tip: "Ice melts as arrows leave."

figure.alt: Level 131 in the Lagoon world: an ice cell showing 5 on a pyramid-shaped board
figure.caption: Level 131 introduces ice.

entries.name: Level-3 rock
entries.summary: The toughest rock: three bomb hits.
what: A level-3 rock has three white dots and needs three bombs. Each hit cracks it and takes a dot away; the third breaks it.
Its bombs come from different arrows, usually from different sides of the rock.
how: Find all three bombs before you start: some are buried deeper than others.
The arrows behind the rock can only go once the last bomb has hit.
notes: Level 161 introduces them with two level-3 rocks and nothing else. From then on about 8% of rocks are level 3, rising to 18% by level 300.

entries.name: Paint tile
entries.summary: Gives an arrow that passes over it its colour.
what: A paint tile is a round splash of colour with that colour's symbol. It never blocks.

An arrow that flies over it takes its colour and symbol for the rest of its path, so it can get through, and open, a gate of that colour further on. Bombs stay bombs. The paint stays for later arrows too.
how: A gate with no arrow of its colour in sight? Look for a paint tile on some arrow's path in front of it.
The tutorial shows an arrow of another colour picking up paint and opening a gate.
notes: Level 191 introduces paint with one tile and the one gate only its paint opens.
In-game tip: "Paint gives an arrow its colour."

figure.alt: Level 191 in the Autumn woods: blue paint tiles on a ring-shaped board
figure.caption: Level 191 introduces paint tiles.

entries.name: Shutter
entries.summary: A roller door that hides arrows until it rolls up.
what: A shutter is a steel roller door over a rectangle of cells, 2×2 to 3×3 at first and up to 5 cells a side later, with a number on a plate. The arrows under it, even partly, are hidden and locked.
No path gets through a shutter that's down. Each time any arrow leaves the board the number drops by one, and at 0 the shutter rolls up and shows what was underneath.
how: Tapping a shutter only rattles it: it costs no heart.

No powerup touches a hidden arrow, because you can't see it. Remove arrow can't take one: tap the shutter with it and nothing is used. Hints, Auto-play and the wand never pick one, and grid lines draw no path for it.
Like ice, the number runs out just as you run out of other arrows, so clear everything that isn't waiting on it.
notes: Level 221 introduces shutters with one, counting from 5. Bigger ones arrive from levels 320 and 420.
In-game tip: "Shutters roll up as arrows leave."

figure.alt: Level 221 in the Crystal caves: a steel shutter with its number on a diamond-shaped board
figure.caption: Level 221 introduces shutters.

entries.name: Two-colour gate
entries.summary: A gate that needs two colours, in order.
what: A two-colour gate holds two symbols: the first on the left and bigger. Its frame shows the colour it lets through next.

At first only the first colour gets through, which uses up its pip. Then the second colour gets through too, and when it passes the gate opens for good. Other colours and bombs bump until then, and colour switches don't open it.
how: Send an arrow of the big symbol's colour first, then one of the small symbol's colour.

If Remove arrow takes an arrow of the second colour whose path runs through the gate before the first colour has passed, its pip is still used: the gate then opens for good as soon as the first colour passes.
notes: Level 251 introduces them with a single two-colour gate.
In-game tip: "Two-colour gate: big symbol goes first."

figure.alt: Level 251 in the Crystal caves: a two-colour gate near the bottom of the board
figure.caption: Level 251 introduces two-colour gates.

entries.name: Chain bomb & rock walls
entries.summary: One blast runs along a whole wall of touching rocks.
what: A chain bomb is a bomb with a spark on every cell of its fuse. Its blast runs through every rock touching the one it hits, and on through the rocks touching those: each takes one hit.

Rock walls are lines of 3 to 8 one-cell rocks, sometimes with one bend. One chain bomb opens the whole wall. A level-2 or level-3 rock in a wall takes one hit from the blast and needs bombs of its own for the rest.
how: Find the chain bomb aimed at the wall and clear its path, like any bomb.
Check the wall for dotted rocks: they need their own bombs as well.
notes: Level 281 introduces walls with one wall of 4 or 5 rocks and its chain bomb. From level 282 every level has at least one wall, and hard levels one more.

figure.alt: The How to play lesson Chain bombs: a wall of three stone rocks and a chain bomb aimed at it
figure.caption: A rock wall and its chain bomb, in How to play.

entries.name: Keys and doors
entries.summary: A key unlocks every door of its colour at once, but not two-colour gates.
what: A key lies on the board in its colour, with that colour's symbol in its bow. On a board with a key, the gates of its colour are locked doors: a double door in the colour with a padlock showing the same symbol. The key never blocks.

The first arrow, or bomb on its way to its rock, that flies over the key turns it: a spark runs to every door of its colour, wherever it is, the padlocks drop and the doors swing open for good. Two-colour gates don't react to keys.
how: A locked door far away with no arrow of its colour in sight? Look for the key of its colour on a free arrow's path.
A key earlier on an arrow's own path unlocks a door further along that same path before the arrow gets there.
notes: Level 311 introduces keys and doors with one key and its doors.
In-game tip: "A key opens every door of its colour."

figure.alt: The How to play lesson Keys and doors: a blue key on a grey plate and a blue locked door with a padlock
figure.caption: Keys and doors in How to play: the key unlocks every door of its colour.

entries.name: Auto-play
entries.summary: Plays a free arrow for you.
what: Auto-play picks an arrow that can leave right now and plays it for you, so it never costs a heart. That can be a bomb whose path to its rock is clear. It never picks an arrow hidden under a shutter.
how: Use it when you're stuck and don't want to spend a heart finding the way.
A pack of 3 costs 100 coins in the shop. It's also a daily-challenge milestone reward.
notes: A run that uses a powerup doesn't go on the leaderboard.

entries.name: Grid lines
entries.summary: Shows the path of every arrow you can see, for 5 seconds.
what: Grid lines draw the lane of every arrow you can see, from its head to the edge, for 5 seconds of play, turning at mirrors and jumping through portals. A bomb's lane ends at the rock it will hit.

A lane is drawn whatever is in the way: if an arrow, a rock, ice, a shutter or a gate of another colour stands on it, that arrow is blocked. Arrows hidden under a shutter get no lane, so the lines don't give them away.
how: Use it on big boards to spot which arrows are free.
A pack of 3 costs 150 coins.
notes: A run that uses a powerup doesn't go on the leaderboard.

entries.name: Remove arrow
entries.summary: Removes any arrow you can see, even a blocked one, without costing a heart.
what: Tap Remove arrow, then tap any arrow you can see: it disappears, even if it was blocked, and you don't lose a heart.

Whatever that arrow would have done on its way out still happens, all along its path, even past whatever blocked it: a bomb hits the first rock on its path, gates of its colour open (the colour it has there, after any paint tile), switches it passes are pressed, a two-colour gate uses up its pip, and every ice block and shutter counts down by one.
how: Save it for the one arrow that blocks everything else.
A pack of 3 costs 250 coins.
notes: It never takes an arrow hidden under a shutter, even partly hidden, because you can't see it. Tapping the shutter only rattles it and tells you hidden arrows can't be removed: nothing is used, and Remove arrow stays ready for an arrow you can see.
A run that uses a powerup doesn't go on the leaderboard.

entries.name: Magic wand
entries.summary: Clears up to 5 free arrows at once.
what: The magic wand clears up to 5 arrows that are free to leave, all at once: the ones nearest the middle of the screen. It never costs a heart.

A bomb with a clear path to its rock counts as free and hits the rock. An arrow hidden under a shutter is never free, so the wand never takes one. Arrows the wand frees stay on the board for your next move.
how: Use it on big boards to thin out the easy arrows quickly, or to count down ice and shutters fast.
A pack of 3 costs 300 coins. It's also the reward for 25 daily challenges in a month.
notes: The shop also sells a bundle with one of each powerup for 200 coins.

entries.name: How to play
entries.icon: <svg viewBox='0 0 48 48'><path d='M8 24h22' stroke='#1C9FD8' stroke-width='7' stroke-linecap='round'/><path d='M42 24l-13-10v20z' fill='#1C9FD8'/></svg>
entries.summary: Tap an arrow with a clear path. Clear the board.
what: Every arrow points somewhere. Tap one and it slides off the board along its path, but only if nothing is in its way. The path runs straight on, except where a mirror turns it or a portal carries it across the board.
Clear every arrow to win the level. Each arrow you clear can only free others, so a level can never become impossible.
how: Start with arrows whose path to the edge is already empty.
Big boards open zoomed in: pinch or scroll to zoom, and drag to move.

figure.alt: Level 33 in the Jungle world: a zigzag board packed with bendy arrows in six colours
figure.caption: Level 33, in the Jungle world.

entries.name: Hearts
entries.summary: You have 3. Tapping a blocked arrow costs one.
what: You start every level with 3 hearts. Tapping an arrow that's blocked costs a heart. When you run out, the attempt is over.
how: When you're out of hearts you can continue once with 100 coins for 3 hearts, or, on Android, watch a video for full hearts. Each continue works once per attempt.
Or tap Retry to start the level again.
notes: A run with a continue doesn't go on the leaderboard.

entries.name: Coins
entries.summary: Earned every level; spent on hints, continues and powerups.
what: You start with 100 coins. Every level pays 10, a hard level 30, and a perfect clear (no mistakes) 5 more. The daily challenge pays 20, plus 5 for perfect, and your first clear of another player's custom map pays 10 to 30.
how: Spend them on hints (30), a continue with 3 hearts (100), and powerup packs in the shop.
Coin packs are also for sale in the app's shop.

figure.alt: The Level complete card: time 00:08, 2 hearts lost, 859 points and +10 coins
figure.caption: Every win pays coins.

entries.name: Hints
entries.icon: <svg viewBox='0 0 48 48'><g fill='#F2B705'><circle cx='24' cy='19.2' r='13.44'/><path d='M17.28 28.8h13.44l-.96 8.64H18.24z'/></g><path d='M20.16 43.2h7.68' stroke='#F2B705' stroke-width='3.84' stroke-linecap='round'/></svg>
entries.summary: Lights up an arrow that can leave right now.
what: A hint highlights an arrow whose path is clear, never one hidden under a shutter. You get 3 free hints; after that a hint costs 30 coins, or, on Android, a short video.
how: Hints are allowed on leaderboard runs, unlike powerups and continues.

entries.name: Hard levels
entries.summary: Every 10th level: bigger, deeper, at night, for 30 coins.
what: Every 10th level, from level 10, is a hard level: about 1.45 times as big as the levels around it, always a picture shape, played at night on a dark board. It keeps the deepest of three boards, so it's always harder than the nine levels before it.
Hard levels get more of the newer obstacles too. The two levels after a hard level are a little smaller, to catch your breath.
how: Zoom out first to see the whole board, then work from the edges in.
A hard level pays 30 coins, plus 5 for a perfect clear.

figure.alt: Hard level 170 at night: a huge dark board packed with arrows
figure.caption: Hard level 170.

entries.name: Board shapes
entries.icon: <svg viewBox='0 0 48 48'><path d='M24 41S6 30 6 17a9 9 0 0 1 18-3 9 9 0 0 1 18 3c0 13-18 24-18 24z' fill='none' stroke='#8C5CF0' stroke-width='3' stroke-dasharray='2 4' stroke-linecap='round'/></svg>
entries.summary: 49 shapes, from hexagons and spirals to rockets and castles.
what: Boards come in 49 shapes. 18 plain shapes stretch to fit the phone: the rectangle, rounded, circle, diamond, cross, notches, holes, ring, hourglass, arch, blob, hexagon, triangle, ell, zigzag, stairs, chevron and spiral. 31 pictures keep their own proportions: heart, star, tree, house, cat, fish, mushroom, cup, butterfly, flower, leaf, flame, gem, lightning, moon, cactus, pyramid, rocket, anchor, boat, crown, key, bell, ghost, snowflake, gear, cloud, candy, acorn, turtle and castle.

Levels 1 to 4 are rectangles; after that only a few are. New shapes unlock a few at a time up to level 100, and many worlds have pictures of their own, like the flame and gem in Volcano or the snowflake in Glacier. The longest board side grows up to 100 cells.
From level 25 about 1 in 6 normal levels is a knot level, where arrows zig-zag at nearly every cell.
how: Holes, notches and narrow parts change which edge an arrow can reach: check the path, not just the direction.
Cells outside the shape are empty space that arrows fly over.

figure.alt: All 49 board shapes as white silhouettes, each at its smallest and largest board size
figure.caption: Every shape at its smallest and largest board, with the level it first appears on.

entries.summary: 17 worlds, each with its own look, on one scrolling map.
what: The levels are split into 17 worlds: Meadow (1–20), Jungle (21–40), Volcano (41–80), Desert (81–100), Lagoon (101–140), Mushroom forest (141–160), Autumn woods (161–200), Glacier (201–220), Crystal caves (221–260), Cherry blossom (261–280), Clockwork town (281–320), Coral reef (321–340), Bayou (341–380), Candy land (381–400), Temple ruins (401–440), Sky islands (441–460) and Starlight (461–500). After level 500 they come round again from Jungle.
Each world has its own scenery, board colours, arrow style and the puff an arrow leaves as it takes off. Hard levels are the same world at night.
how: The map is the home screen: scroll it, tap a finished level to play it again, or tap Play for the next one.
Replays don't pay coins. Winning a world's last level opens the next world.

entries.summary: One board a day, the same for everyone, with monthly rewards.
what: Each calendar day has one board, the same for every player. It's harder later in the week, and it has no obstacles.
You can play any day of the current month up to today. Only the first win of each day pays: 20 coins, plus 5 for perfect.
how: Days you complete count towards this month's milestones: 2 days: 50 coins · 7 days: 100 coins · 13 days: 150 coins and an Auto-play · 19 days: 200 coins and a Grid lines · 25 days: 300 coins and a Magic wand.
Progress starts again each month.
notes: Daily runs don't go on the level leaderboards.

figure.alt: The daily challenge calendar for October 2026, with the monthly milestone bar above it
figure.caption: This month's calendar and milestones.

entries.name: Leaderboards & profiles
entries.icon: <svg viewBox='0 0 48 48'><rect x='6' y='22' width='11' height='18' rx='3' fill='#1C9FD8'/><rect x='18.5' y='12' width='11' height='28' rx='3' fill='#F2B705'/><rect x='31' y='27' width='11' height='13' rx='3' fill='#FF6B6B'/></svg>
entries.summary: A board for every level, plus four global boards.
what: Each level has its own leaderboard, ranked by fewest hearts lost, then by the fastest time. You see the top 10 and your own row.
Only clean runs count: no continue and no powerup. Hints are fine. Your best run stays on the board.

The Global tab ranks everyone on four boards: Score (points for every level won), Perfect (levels won without losing a heart), Maps (other players' custom maps cleared) and Creators (plays of your own maps). The top 100 of each are also on the website's global ranking page.

Your score: each level you win is worth 1,000 points, less 25 for each heart lost and less for the time taken (scaled by the size of the board), and never less than 100. A win with a continue or a powerup is worth 100; hints don't cost points. Each level keeps the most points you have earned on it, so replaying a level can only raise your score.
how: The first time you open a leaderboard you can pick a username (3 to 16 letters, digits or _) and one of 12 avatars. A name is yours for good once saved. Without one you show as "Player" and a short code.
Tap any row to see that player's profile: their stats and published maps.
On Android, players signed in with Play Games can use a picture of their own; every picture is checked before anyone sees it.
Settings → Profile → "Delete my leaderboard data" removes your name, picture, results and stats.

entries.name: Play with friends
entries.summary: Race 2 to 8 players on the same boards with a room code.
what: Home → Play with friends → Create room makes a 6-character code. Friends join by typing it, scanning the invite's QR code or opening the invite link, in the app or in the browser.
The host picks the difficulty (Easy, Medium, Hard or Expert) and how many games to play, up to 20. Every game is a new board, the same for everyone, after a 3-2-1 countdown.
how: Clear the board fastest: the first to finish scores the most points. Out of hearts or out of time scores 0.
Once someone finishes, the others get as long again as they took, at least a minute.
Rooms have no powerups, hints, restarts, continues or ads. After the last game a podium shows the winners, and the host can start Play again.
notes: Rooms need a profile name, so everyone can see who's who.

The invite link joins the room by itself: in the app on an Android phone that has Exitwise, and in the browser game on a computer or an iPhone. An Android phone without the app offers the browser game or Google Play.

entries.name: Custom maps
entries.icon: <svg viewBox='0 0 48 48'><rect x='6' y='6' width='36' height='36' rx='8' fill='#FF922B'/><path d='M18 10v28M30 10v28M10 18h28M10 30h28' stroke='#FFFDF8' stroke-width='2' opacity='.6'/><path d='M14 34l3-9 16-16 6 6-16 16z' fill='#3B3355'/><path d='M14 34l3-9 6 6z' fill='#FFFDF8'/></svg>
entries.summary: Build your own levels, and play other players' maps.
what: Custom maps, on the level map, opens players' own levels: browse Popular, New and Top rated, search by name or share code, and filter by size and difficulty.
Each map has its own leaderboard, a rating and a clear rate. Your first clear of another player's map pays 10 to 30 coins, depending on how hard it is.
how: In the editor, pick a size (5 to 40 cells each way), one of 49 starting shapes, plain ones or pictures (a picture starts big enough to show whole), and one of the 17 world looks, by day or by night.

The tray has four groups of tools. Draw: the board's cells, arrows in six colours, bombs and chain bombs, and the eraser. Blocks: rocks of level 1, 2 or 3, ice and shutters. Colours: gates, two-colour gates, paint tiles and colour switches. Paths: mirrors and portal pairs.

Above the tools, the strip holds the picked tool's settings: a colour, a rock's level, the number of arrows ice or a shutter waits for, a mirror's slant or the kind of bomb. Tap a block with its own tool to give it those settings, or to turn a mirror. A portal pair is a drag from one end to the other, or two taps.
The check bar tells you straight away when an arrow can never leave or a block breaks a rule, and rates the map from Easy to Expert.
Test your map: you have to clear it yourself before you can publish it with a share code.
Every map follows the map rules. From a map's page you can report it or hide a creator's maps.
notes: Every block works in a map just as it does in the levels: each one has its own page in this wiki.
In the editor, shutters are see-through, so you can see the arrows they hide. A map has at most 6 portal pairs, and ice and shutters count up to 99.
A map with chain bombs, level-2 or level-3 rocks, paint tiles, two-colour gates or switches needs the latest version of Exitwise: older versions can't play it.
